fields.v: Not an SDD approach. Yuj coding-agent harness (author's, github.com/sydches/yuj; version Not stated): treatment package = half-life working-view rule (older tool results shortened in stages once prompt reaches 50% of window) + stall detector with fixed interventions + command safeguards; control = same harness with full chronological transcript. Pro and FeatureBench pressure runs used an earlier frozen treatment version

Harness: Yuj (control vs treatment). Qwen3.6 served locally with llama-server, 4-bit Q4 K XL weights; transfer models each with a declared four-bit weight file and model-specific serving settings; greedy decoding; one trajectory per task per arm; fixed 480-s attempt budget. Metrics: resolution (benchmark evaluator accepts the task) and mean per-task F2PF; turns, prompt tokens, wall time for pressure comparisons. Success is defined per task (p. 7); no success criterion for a configuration is stated by the authors.

fields.why: Round 2 gave works/partly/does-not-work verdicts from its own cut-off (resolution share >=50% / 20-50% / <20%, admitted in its 'why') and cost 'works' with no basis. The paper defines success per task (evaluator accepts the task; F2PF, p. 7) but states no success criterion for a configuration, so per the 2026-11-23 rule every verdict is 'no criterion stated by the authors'. Also fixed the probe entry: the paper says no altered setting improved resolution beyond the rerun difference and every Qwen3.6 variant was lower (p. 23), not that probes 'never beat' the frozen settings (Devstral activation 0.25/protect 2 gave 2/15 vs 1/15). Other values re-checked against Tables 7-9, 11, 18 (pp. 17-19, 23)

fields.v: Paired: every task run once under control and once under treatment; same task, model weights, context capacity, tool interface, serving, evaluator, harness code; differ only in one checked-in configuration package. Context windows varied (Verified 20,480 / 43,008 / 262,144; Pro 49,152 / 262,144; FeatureBench 47,104 / 262,144). Baseline: control configuration. Acceptance tests: benchmark F2P tests. Repetitions: 1 greedy trajectory per arm. Human intervention: none. Isolation: no network, no gold patches. Operating point set during earlier development on same benchmark families (not held-out)

Under context pressure treatment beats control on F2PF in all three benchmarks (Verified +21.1 pp [14.1, 28.3], Pro +17.5, FeatureBench +9.1; all p<0.0001) and on resolution on Verified (+29 tasks) and Pro (+41); after Holm (repository level) Verified and FeatureBench resolution not significant. Gains shrink with window size; near zero at 262,144 on Verified and Pro. Transfer: gains for all models (1.5x-2.1x F2PF). Reading boundary stretched 2.21-2.53x. Treatment used 2-6x more turns/tokens/time under pressure

Yes: paired design distinguished configurations under pressure; not under ample context. Repeatable: single greedy trajectory per arm, run-to-run variation not measured; Verified windows collected successively (window confounded with run era); Pro/FeatureBench wide-window rows from earlier packages. Limitation stated: estimates the whole package, not single rules; not compute-matched

Effect of the whole treatment package only; not compute-matched; one trajectory per arm; four locally served 4-bit open-weight models (no hosted frontier models); repository-level coding tasks only; no human quality judgment; shared pretraining exposure; compared only with full-transcript control, not summaries or retrieval. Future: detector-only component study, time-only variation, adaptive harness, read caching, model design x context

Yuj harness, configs, experimental contract, provenance and paired task outcomes public (github.com/sydches/yuj); benchmark lists, evaluators and raw runs not public.
